evidence.source: Hong Kong Educational University, Lexicon of Chinese Phonology: Richi (貴)
evidence.text: The page presents oracle-bone, bronze, small-seal, and standard forms; it describes the early forms as hands holding earth, assigns 貝 a semantic role and 中 a phonetic role, and lists Cantonese gwai3 and Mandarin gui4 for the basic sense ‘high price’. This is the page’s analysis, not a consensus account.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 - 貴

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, transcribing 說文解字 and Duan Yucai’s commentary
evidence.text: The transmitted 說文 account glosses 貴 as ‘not cheap’, analyzes it as 从貝臾聲, and says 臾 is an ancient form of 蕢. Duan’s commentary gives 居胃切. This records the dictionary’s analysis; it does not independently establish the original graph’s depicted components.
evidence.title: 說文解字「貴」

evidence.source: Wikisource, transmitted 說文解字 text
evidence.text: In the 貝 section, 說文 explains 貝 as a shell and says shells served as currency before coin use. It defines 貴 as ‘not cheap’, analyzes it from 貝 with 臾 as phonetic, and identifies 臾 as an ancient form of 蕢. These are historical lexicographic assertions, not proof of early graphic motivation.
evidence.title: 說文解字/06

evidence.source: Kim Jun-su, Korea Journal of Chinese Linguistics (2016), article record and abstract
evidence.text: The abstract argues 貴 and 遺 have distinct graphic and phonological origins; it analyzes 貴 as 貝 plus 臾, described as the protoform of 簣, functioning phonically. It proposes Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese *kluds for 貴 and reports a modified Baxter–Sagart proposal *kut-s. These are reconstructions, not attested ancient pronunciations.
evidence.title: 《說文解字》貴聲系字의 上古音 再構에 대한 小考

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The editorial note says 䝿 is a direct regularization of the 說文 small-seal form. It also discusses later variant shapes as possible graphic corruptions, including an upper component being distorted in transmission. This concerns later written variants, not evidence for the earliest graph’s original depiction.

search_audit.outcome: Search confirmed a Ministry result on the general 1956 simplification program and an official variant dictionary account of 䝿 and later graphic change. Character-specific listing for 贵 was not confirmed from the opened official page.

gaps: No primary inscription corpus entry or artifact image was opened to establish the earliest attestation of 貴 or its earliest use. Search-result claims that it first appears in bronze inscriptions and occurs in a Warring States tomb phrase remain unverified.

The early graphic interpretation is disputed: the Hong Kong Educational University reference describes hands holding earth and assigns 中 as phonetic; 說文 and the 2016 phonology study analyze 貝 plus 臾. The evidence gathered does not resolve the original depiction or establish which account best explains early forms.

The role of 臾 is well-attested as a traditional dictionary and scholarly analysis, and the 2016 abstract associates it with the protoform of 簣. Its exact historical sound correspondence to 貴 is not fully established by a comparative series in this research. In Zhengzhang Shangfang’s system the study reports 貴 *kluds and series member 匱 *gruds, 蕢 *gruds / *kʰruːds, and 臾 *gruds; it separately reports modified Baxter–Sagart 貴 *kut-s and 匱 *grut-s. No direct ancient pronunciation is known.

No independently dated primary lexical attestations were inspected. Classical quotations reported by a secondary dictionary suggest price, rank, and esteem/value uses, but they do not establish the chronology or semantic pathway among these senses.

The modern readings Mandarin guì/gui4 and Cantonese gwai3 are externally listed, but a same-system historical reconstruction for both 貴 and the proposed phonetic component was not independently assembled.
The 1956 general simplification date is reported by the official search result, but the exact official table entry for 贵 and a pre-1956 attestation of this exact form were not verified.

No historical glyph candidates are included because Commons search did not establish a candidate with sufficiently clear identity and reuse provenance, and Xiaoxuetang’s character-specific direct image query was inaccessible. No image pixels were inspected.

The dossier’s Tibetan comparison was not verified; it should not be treated as established etymology. No whole-character phonetic-loan proposal was confirmed, and the early-form dispute concerns graphic analysis rather than a demonstrated borrowing.

limitations.text: No candidate image is proposed: a Commons search did not establish a suitable reusable 貴 glyph image, Xiaoxuetang’s CC0-covered query output could not be retrieved with an exact record page and supplied form label, and the alternative Academia Sinica chardb page explicitly restricts reuse. No image was visually inspected.
